title: LLM Output Audit and Customer Ops Handbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
-------
This playbook defines the program and operational runbook for periodic LLM output audits performed during enterprise onboarding, and for recurring quality audits that feed QBRs and escalation flow. The document is intended for Customer Success Engineers, Support Engineers, Solutions Architects, and SREs who participate in customer-facing quality investigations and acceptance checks.

Goals
-----
- Provide a repeatable, low-friction audit process that verifies model fidelity, prompt safety, latency/cost trade-offs, and business-relevant correctness for enterprise customers.
- Map telemetry assertions to customer SLAs and QBR artifacts so audits directly inform action items and supplier-level escalations.
- Establish clear roles, ownership, and timelines for audit, remediation, and customer communication.

Scope
-----
This handbook covers:
- Acceptance audits performed during the first 30 days after tenant provisioning.
- Monthly stability and fidelity audits for Dedicated and Private tenants.
- Ad-hoc investigation audits triggered by customer reports or anomaly alerts.
It does NOT cover: low-level kernel performance tuning (eng-serving-runtime), legal data-exposure forensics (security-and-compliance), or billing disputes (finance-and-legal).

Key Definitions
---------------
- Audit Run: a discrete execution of the audit harness over a defined prompt set and telemetry window.
- Golden Prompt Set: a customer-specific set of 50–250 canonical prompts provided by product/CS and derived from customer workflows.
- Fidelity Score: weighted metric combining semantic-match (embedding cosine), hallucination rate, and instruction-following pass/fail.
- Telemetry Assertions: measurable signals (latency p95, token cost per request, model mismatch rate) that must meet thresholds.

Ownership and Roles
-------------------
- Customer Success Engineer (CSE): primary owner of the audit schedule, customer comms, and acceptance criteria.
- Support Engineer (Tier 2): executes the audit, collects artifacts, and runs the evaluation harness.
- Platform SRE: verifies infrastructure signals (GPU preemption, KV cache hit-rates, batching behaviour).
- Applied ML / Model Onboarding: interprets fidelity regressions and recommends model or quantization adjustments.
- Escalation Liaison (CS lead): coordinates cross-team escalation and external SLAs.

Audit Types and Cadence
-----------------------
1) Day-0 Acceptance Audit (CSE + Support Engineer)
   - When: within 72 hours of tenant provisioning or cutover.
   - Scope: golden prompt set x baseline model + production routing config.
   - Outputs: acceptance report PDF, pass/fail gate, action list.
   - Decision: if critical failures (>10% catastrophic hallucinations or SLA breaches), pause cutover and invoke go-live safety net.

2) 30-Day Stability Audit (CSE + Platform SRE + Applied ML)
   - When: 30 days after provision and monthly thereafter for Dedicated/Private customers.
   - Scope: extended prompt set, synthetic traffic replay at 10th/50th/90th percentile concurrency.
   - Outputs: fidelity and economics dashboard snapshot, model-version drift check.

3) Ad-hoc Investigation Audit (Support Engineer)
   - When: triggered by customer-reported issue, automated fidelity alert, or QBR signal.
   - Scope: focused prompt subset plus relevant request traces and telemetry window.
   - Outputs: RCA outline, mitigation steps, recommended rollback or model-variant switch.

Audit Preconditions and Prerequisites
------------------------------------
- Golden Prompt Set approved and stored in the customer workspace (S3 path or internal asset id).
- Synthetic traffic harness referencing the tenant’s routing and model pinning configuration.
- Access to tenant metrics: request traces, model selection logs, KV cache metrics, latency histograms, and cost-by-token metrics.
- List of acceptance thresholds agreed in the contract or QBR baseline.

Audit Procedure (step-by-step)
------------------------------
1. Prepare environment (Support Engineer)
   - Pull latest golden prompt set: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-customer-assets/<tenant-id>/golden-prompts.json ./prompts.json
   - Confirm model pins: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/tenants/<tenant>/config | jq .model_pin
   - Validate telemetry window: ensure 72h of request logs and metric retention is available.

2. Run fidelity harness
   - Run: python3 tools/audit_runner.py --prompts ./prompts.json --tenant <tenant> --samples 3 --output ./audit-artifacts/<date>/
   - Collect: generated outputs, per-sample embeddings, similarity scores, hallucination annotations.

3. Score and thresholding (Support Engineer + Applied ML)
   - Compute: semantic-match (cosine >= 0.78), hallucination-rate <= 5%, exact-instruction-following >= 90% (values gated per-customer).
   - Generate: PDF audit-summary including top-10 failures, example traces, and per-route latency/cost tables.

4. Telemetry correlation (Platform SRE)
   - Confirm: p50/p95 latency meets SLOs (p95 < 450ms for interactive tier; verify if dedicated private SLO differs).
   - Check: KV cache hit-rate, batch sizes distribution, and preemption logs around audit windows.

5. Draft customer-facing report (CSE)
   - Include: executive summary, pass/fail status, actionable remediation items, and expected timeline.
   - Template snippets: see "Customer Communication Templates" below.

Evaluation Metrics and Thresholds (example table)
---------------------------------------------------
- Fidelity Score: pass if > 0.85 (weighted).
- Semantic Match (embedding cosine): median >= 0.78.
- Hallucination Rate: <= 5% of prompts flagged as hallucinated.
- Instruction-Following: >= 90% pass on binary checks.
- Token Cost Delta vs baseline: <= +15% acceptable for first-30-day period.
- p95 Completion Latency: Dedicated <= 400ms, Hosted Interactive <= 450ms.

Customer Communication Templates
--------------------------------
- Initial Audit Notification (CSE)
  Subject: Audit scheduled: LLM output acceptance for <tenant-name>
  Body snippet: "We will run the agreed acceptance tests on <date>. Expected duration 2–4 hours. We will share an executive summary and remediation items within 24 hours."

- Failure Triage Notification (CSE)
  Subject: Action required: fidelity issues detected in acceptance audit for <tenant-name>
  Body snippet: "We observed elevated hallucination rates on prompts related to <feature>. We recommend activating fallback model-variant B and scheduling a joint trial with Applied ML. See attached artifacts and proposed timeline."

Escalation Matrix and SLA Intervals
-----------------------------------
- Severity P1 (customer-critical production degradation): contact sequence within 30 minutes; full incident bridge within 60 minutes. Owner: Customer Success lead + Platform SRE.
- Severity P2 (functional regressions impacting >10% of workflows): initial contact within 2 hours; remediation plan within 24 hours. Owner: Support Engineering.
- Severity P3 (cosmetic or minor discrepancies): reply within 48 hours; plan when convenient. Owner: CSE.

Automations and Tooling
-----------------------
- Audit harness: tools/audit_runner.py – supports parallel sampling, synthetic replay, and per-sample annotation export.
- Eval dashboard: internal Grafana panel "Customer Audit - <tenant>" with prebuilt panels for fidelity, latency, cost, and model-variant distribution.
- Alerting: fidelity-regression alert triggers a JIRA with labels audit-regression/<tenant>.

Acceptance Gates and Decisioning
--------------------------------
- Gate PASS: CSE marks tenant as "accepted-for-prod" in provisioning tracker and proceeds with final cutover.
- Gate FAIL (critical): pause further traffic increases; open cross-team incident and enforce rollback to previously pinned model-variant.
- Gate FAIL (non-critical): schedule remediation backlog item with delivery SLA aligned to customer's support tier (e.g., 7 days for standard, 3 days for enterprise).

Post-Audit Remediation Playbook
-------------------------------
1. Identify root cause category: prompt drift, model regression, quantization artifact, infra contention, or routing mismatch.
2. Short-term mitigations: swap to a verified model-variant, apply prompt transformations, increase KV cache segment retention, or throttle concurrency.
3. Medium-term fixes: coordinate with Applied ML on model re-finetune, with eng-serving-runtime on quantization reprofile, or with Platform SRE for capacity adjustments.
4. Confirm fix via focused re-run of the failed prompt subset and update the audit artifacts.

QBR Integration and Artifacts
-----------------------------
- Include audit-pass/fail trend (last 6 months), top recurring failure classes, and cost-per-1000-requests delta.
- Provide a prioritized remediation roadmap with owners and expected impact estimate (latency, fidelity, cost).
- Recommended QBR slide deck sections: Executive Summary, Fidelity Trend, Synthetic Suite Results, Proposed Actions.

Example CLI snippets and queries
-------------------------------
- Retrieve top failed prompts by fidelity score:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://internal-api.redwood.ai/audit/failures?tenant=<tenant>&days=30 | jq .results | head -n 20

- Run local audit harness sample command:
  python3 tools/audit_runner.py --prompts ./prompts.json --tenant acme-corp --samples 5 --parallel 8 --output ./audit-artifacts/2026-11-02/

Documented Known Failure Modes and Workarounds
----------------------------------------------
- Symptom: Intermittent semantic drop concentrated on long-context prompts.
  Root cause: KV cache eviction policy misaligned with production sequence lengths.
  Workaround: Increase KV cache retention window for the tenant (Platform SRE).

- Symptom: Elevated token cost after quantized model upgrade.
  Root cause: quantization configuration caused longer decode paths in certain layers.
  Workaround: Revert to prior quantization profile or apply selective dequantization for last layers.

Audit Schedule Template (example table)
--------------------------------------
- Day 0: Acceptance Audit (CSE + Support) – 72 hours post provisioning
- Day 30: Stability Audit (CSE + Platform SRE + Applied ML)
- Monthly: Synthetic pass/fail slice for Dedicated/Private tenants
- On trigger: Ad-hoc audit within SLA per escalation matrix

Attachments and Artifacts to Include with Every Audit
----------------------------------------------------
- Prompts used (golden set)
- Generated outputs (JSONL) with trace ids
- Embeddings and similarity matrix CSV
- Telemetry window export (request logs, model-selection logs)
- Audit summary PDF and action items list

Metrics for Continuous Improvement
----------------------------------
- Mean time from audit failure to mitigation deployed (target < 72 hours for P1/P2).
- Fraction of audits that require model-variant rollback (target < 5%).
- Customer satisfaction score on audit process (CSAT target > 4.3/5).

Appendix: Escalation Contact Template
-------------------------------------
- Incident bridge: #customer-incident-<tenant> on Slack (create at start)
- Pager: Platform SRE on-call (follow sequence in oncall-and-incident-response)
- Escalation email alias: cs-escalations@redwood.ai

References
----------
- Internal audit harness README: /docs/internal/tools/audit_runner.md
